real_conflicts: The typography critic's proposal to apply a vertical skew or italicization to the headline is a direct violation of my mandate. Introducing a mechanical distortion to the typeface introduces a 'generic motion effect' that has no relationship to the performance's specific physicality. It undermines the sophisticated, static tension of the current layout and turns the typography into a cliché rather than a structural anchor.

The visual concept critic's demand to make the figure 'anatomically suggestive' with a clear spine and limbs risks destroying the abstract, gestural quality that allows the figure to function as a pure spatial counterweight. Over-defining the form will make it a literal illustration rather than a compositional element, potentially making it visually cluttered and harder to balance against the clean typography.
accepted: The visual concept critic's insistence that the figure must occupy a larger portion of the canvas (40-50% height) aligns perfectly with my critique that the figure is currently visually subordinate. Scaling it up is the primary mechanism for restoring the necessary focal dominance.

The color critic's suggestion to apply a soft-edge gradient or blur to the figure's strokes is a strong compositional tool. It will help the figure emerge from the negative space rather than sitting on top of it, creating a sense of atmospheric depth that bridges the gap between the figure and the central void.
concession: I concede that the current 'passive' relationship between the text and figure is not just a matter of scale, but also of energy. While I reject the skew, I accept that the figure needs to be more dynamic in its placement to actively 'push' against the text block, rather than just sitting in the corner.
compromise: We will scale the figure up by 35% and shift it upward and leftward so its upper arc enters the central negative space, creating a direct visual counterweight to the title. Simultaneously, we will apply the color critic's soft-edge treatment to the figure to help it blend into the background glow, and we will adopt the typography critic's suggestion to increase the tracking on the word 'AIR' to create a visual 'lightness' that contrasts with the 'weight' of the figure, without distorting the typeface itself.
nonnegotiable: The high-contrast, static serif typography must remain rigid and upright. Any attempt to mechanically distort the typeface to simulate motion is unacceptable and must be rejected.
